recipes.name: Mustard Fish Curry
recipes.health_benefit: This recipe is rich in Omega-3 fatty acids (from fish) which may help support healthy triglyceride and HDL levels. It also provides Vitamin D and lean protein.
instructions: Marinate fish with a pinch of turmeric and salt. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Grind yellow and black mustard seeds, garlic, and green chilies with a little water to a fine paste.
Heat mustard oil in a pan. Fry the fish pieces lightly until golden on both sides, then remove and set aside.
In the same oil, add chopped onion and sauté until translucent.
Add turmeric, red chili, and coriander powder, cook for a minute.
Add the ground mustard paste and tomato puree. Cook until the oil separates, stirring frequently.
Add 1 cup of water, bring to a simmer. Gently add the fried fish pieces.
Cover and cook for 5-7 minutes until fish is cooked through and gravy thickens. Garnish with fresh coriander.

recipes.name: Ragi Dosa with Sambar
recipes.health_benefit: Ragi is a whole grain rich in fiber and complex carbohydrates, which may help in stabilizing blood glucose and HbA1c levels. Sambar provides plant-based protein and additional fiber from vegetables.

ingredients.item: Light cooking oil (e.g., sunflower or groundnut)

instructions: Grind soaked urad dal and fenugreek seeds to a smooth paste with a little water.
In a large bowl, mix ragi flour, rice flour, and the ground urad dal paste. Add salt and water gradually to make a smooth batter of pouring consistency (like crepe batter).
Cover and let it ferment in a warm place for 6-8 hours or overnight. It should rise slightly.
Heat a non-stick tawa (griddle) over medium heat. Lightly grease it with oil.
Pour a ladleful of batter onto the center of the tawa and spread it in a circular motion to make a thin dosa.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges. Cook until crisp and golden brown on one side.
Serve hot with Sambar and Coconut Chutney.

recipes.name: Masala Omelette with Bell Peppers
recipes.health_benefit: Eggs are an excellent source of protein, Vitamin D, and Vitamin B12. Bell peppers provide Vitamin C, which aids iron absorption, supporting healthy hemoglobin levels. This can contribute to healthy HDL levels.
instructions: Crack eggs into a bowl. Add chopped onion, bell pepper, green chili, coriander leaves, turmeric powder, salt, and black pepper.
Whisk well until all ingredients are combined and frothy.
Heat ghee or oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour the egg mixture into the pan, spreading it evenly.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until the edges set and the bottom is golden brown.
Carefully flip the omelette and cook for another 1-2 minutes until cooked through.
Fold the omelette in half and serve hot.

recipes.name: Oats & Vegetable Khichdi
recipes.health_benefit: Oats and vegetables are excellent sources of fiber and complex carbohydrates, which are beneficial for managing blood sugar (HbA1c, glucose) and supporting healthy cholesterol levels. It's a light yet nutritious meal.
instructions: Heat ghee or oil in a pressure cooker or deep pot.
Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Add onion and sauté until translucent.
Add ginger-garlic paste and green chili, cook for a minute until aromatic.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft. Then add turmeric powder and garam masala, cook for another minute.
Add mixed vegetables and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Add rolled oats, water, and salt. Mix well.
If using a pressure cooker, cook for 1 whistle. If using a pot, cover and simmer for 10-12 minutes until oats are cooked and water is absorbed. Adjust water if needed for desired consistency.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot.

recipes.name: Chicken and Spinach Curry (Palak Chicken)
recipes.health_benefit: This dish is rich in lean protein (chicken), which is beneficial for muscle maintenance and satiety. Spinach (palak) provides iron, supporting healthy hemoglobin levels, and other vital micronutrients.
instructions: Marinate chicken with a pinch of turmeric, salt, and ginger-garlic paste for 15 minutes.
Heat mustard oil or ghee in a pan. Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste and green chilies, cook for a minute.
Add tomato puree, cumin powder, coriander powder, and turmeric powder. Cook until oil separates.
Add marinated chicken and cook until it changes color and is lightly browned.
Stir in the spinach puree and a little water if needed to adjust consistency. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook for 10-15 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through.
Add garam masala and stir. Check seasoning and adjust salt.
Garnish with fresh cream (if using) and serve hot with Jowar Roti or Brown Rice.

recipes.name: Sprouted Moong Dal Chaat
recipes.health_benefit: Sprouted moong dal is high in fiber and plant-based protein, which helps with satiety, blood sugar management, and digestive health. It's a nutrient-dense, refreshing snack.
instructions: Boil or steam the sprouted moong dal lightly for 5-7 minutes until slightly tender but still crunchy. Drain and let it cool.
In a mixing bowl, combine the cooled sprouted moong dal, chopped onion, tomato, cucumber, green chili, and fresh coriander leaves.
Add lemon juice, chaat masala, and black salt. Toss everything gently until well combined.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds if desired.
Serve fresh as a healthy and refreshing snack.

recipes.name: Besan Cheela with Fenugreek Leaves (Methi)
recipes.health_benefit: Besan (gram flour) provides plant-based protein and fiber, aiding satiety and blood sugar regulation. Fenugreek leaves (methi) are known to have properties that may help in glucose metabolism, supporting stable HbA1c and glucose levels.
instructions: In a bowl, combine besan, chopped fenugreek leaves, onion, green chili, grated ginger, turmeric powder, red chili powder, cumin powder, and salt.
Gradually add water and whisk to form a smooth, lump-free batter of pouring consistency, similar to a pancake batter.
Heat a non-stick tawa (griddle) over medium heat and lightly grease it with oil or ghee.
Pour a ladleful of batter onto the tawa and spread it evenly in a circular motion to form a cheela.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until the bottom turns golden brown and the edges start to crisp.
Flip the cheela and cook on the other side for 2-3 minutes until cooked through.
Serve hot with mint chutney or plain yogurt.
